title: Return Shipping Fee When Units Are Rejected at Inspection
content:
Units rejected at inspection earn no refund, so the Returns & Exchanges return shipping fee follows what inspection accepted. A return whose every unit was rejected has nothing refunded to withhold it from.

## Accepted share

| Inspection outcomes on the return | Return shipping fee |
|---|---|
| Every unit rejected | Nothing is withheld |
| Some units rejected | Scaled by the units accepted divided by the units inspected |
| No unit rejected | Withheld in full |

- **Units accepted:** units with the outcome accepted or accepted with fee.
- **Units inspected:** all units on the return's inspection entries, including rejected and missing units.
- The share multiplies the return shipping fee before the fee is rounded to the cent.

## Questions on the rule

**Four units were inspected and three accepted. What share of the fee is withheld?** Three divided by four, 0.75 of it. (Hypothetical figures.)

**One unit was accepted with fee and one rejected.** The unit accepted with fee counts as accepted: one divided by two, 0.5.

**Both units were missing from the parcel.** Missing units are rejected, so every unit was rejected and nothing is withheld.
